data.title: Tesla wants to make its own solar-grade polysilicon at US$3.1 billion Texas plant
data.description:
Tesla is considering a US$3.1 billion polysilicon refinery in Nueces County, Texas, that would give the company a U.S. source for one of the key materials used to make solar cells.

A new filing puts the proposed facility near Robstown, with construction slated to start in 2027 and commercial operations targeted for 2030.

The refinery would give Tesla a way to make one of its own raw materials for solar manufacturing. The plant would turn ultra-pure trichlorosilane into solar-grade polysilicon, which can then be used to make high-efficiency N-type solar cells.

According to Tesla’s filing, China currently accounts for more than 90% of the world’s supply of solar-grade polysilicon. (h/t: Sawyer Merritt)

The filing adds another piece to Tesla’s solar plans in Texas. As Drive Tesla reported last week, site work is already underway in Fort Bend County for Project Crystal Sun, Tesla’s proposed solar cell and panel factory.

Tesla says the Texas investment depends on a tax agreement

The US$3.1 billion proposal is just that, and nothing has been approved. The company says it will only build the refinery in Texas if it secures a deal under the state’s JETI program, which would limit the property value used to calculate local school district operating taxes.

If the project goes ahead, Tesla expects to spend most of the money in 2028 and 2029. The filing estimates construction would support an average of 1,770 jobs a year across Texas from 2027 through 2030, including about 550 directly tied to the build.

Tesla plans to hire its first 260 refinery employees in 2030 and bring that number to 515 by 2032. The filing estimates the project would generate about US$63.5 billion in economic activity across Texas through 2065, with roughly US$61 billion coming from refinery operations.

data.title: Polestar 4 update adds Android 15 and Camping mode, but skips V2L in Canada
data.description:
Polestar is rolling out a significant over-the-air (OTA) update for the Polestar 4 that adds Camping mode, upgrades the infotainment system to Android 15 and lets more owners use their phone as a key. The update, version P4.3.0, also adds Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) in most markets, with Canada, the U.S. and South Korea excluded.

When Polestar announced the Polestar 4 SUV for Canada in September, it said V2L would arrive in a future software update. The feature is now rolling out in other markets, where owners can plug an adapter into the charge port to draw up to 3.3 kW from the battery.

However, Polestar’s press release specifically excludes Canada, and the wording makes it unlikely V2L will ever make it to North America. “Vehicle-to-Load will not be available in the US, Canada and South Korea,” the automaker said.

Canadian owners still get Camping mode, which keeps the cabin at a set temperature and leaves the USB and 12-volt outlets powered while parked. There’s also a new Valet mode that lets owners set a speed limit, lock the glovebox and restrict access to vehicle settings.

The Polestar 4 launched in Canada with Google built into its infotainment system. The move to Android Automotive OS 15 makes the system more responsive, according to Polestar. The update also speeds up vehicle startup, improves Google Maps’ energy estimates and adds a shortcut from the Dashcam app to saved footage.

Owners with compatible Google and Samsung phones will be able to lock, unlock and start their Polestar 4 from their phone, joining iPhone users who got digital key support in 2025. Polestar will send primary drivers an activation code when the feature goes live in their market.

For 2026 and 2027 models with the Pilot pack, the update also adds Park Assist Pilot. Once the driver selects and confirms a perpendicular parking space on the centre screen, the car handles steering and braking. New Polestar 4 vehicles come with P4.3.0 already installed.

data.title: Tesla Assisted Driving gets stricter driver monitoring rules in Europe
data.description:
Tesla has received approval for another round of changes to Tesla Assisted Driving (TAD) in Europe, introducing stricter driver monitoring requirements and requiring drivers to keep their hands on the steering wheel at higher speeds.

The Netherlands Vehicle Authority (RDW) announced this week that it had approved the latest changes, less than two weeks after granting approval for an update that reduced the system’s maximum speed margin from 50% to 10%.

Stricter driver monitoring

Under the latest update, Tesla owners using Assisted Driving at speeds above 130 km/h will be required to keep their hands on the steering wheel. Drivers will also receive warnings sooner if the system detects they are not paying attention, and will receive a “full strike” if they are inattentive while the vehicle is performing a maneuver.

Tesla has also made changes to how the system communicates its speed settings, including notifying drivers when Contextual Max Speed is being used.

Increasing the maximum speed beyond what the system indicates will now require confirmation using the scroll wheel. If the vehicle subsequently exceeds the indicated speed limit, the speed limit icon will pulse red.

As with the previous update, the changes apply to vehicles equipped with Hardware 4 (HW4) or newer and will be delivered through an over-the-air (OTA) software update.

European approval process continues

The RDW conducted testing on public roads and a test track before extending its existing approval, finding no unintended effects on the system’s operation or driving behaviour.

The regulator has notified all 10 countries that have adopted its approval, with Finland joining countries such as Latvia and Slovakia.

The latest changes come just weeks before a potential EU-wide vote in December, with Tesla having already secured support from two of Europe’s largest markets, Germany and Italy.

While 11 countries, including the Netherlands, have now approved the system individually, the date of the EU-wide vote has yet to be formally confirmed.

data.title: Acura issues OTA recall for 14,648 ZDX EVs over potential loss of brake pressure
data.description:
Acura is recalling 14,648 model-year 2024 ZDX electric SUVs in the United States because a software error can briefly reduce or cut brake pressure at low speeds. The recall covers all-wheel drive models built from December 19, 2023, through January 22, 2025, while rear-wheel drive versions are excluded.

The new recall expands a prior 2024 recall that covered 4,174 ZDXs, bringing the number of vehicles listed in the latest campaign to more than three times the original figure.

Transport Canada has yet to issue a similar recall.

Why the ZDX can lose brake pressure

According to Honda’s filing, the problem can occur when several things happen at once. If a driver brakes lightly while turning over uneven pavement, then releases and reapplies the pedal, the brake controller can miscalculate the vehicle’s speed.

On pavement with good grip, that bad reading can make the system think the wheels are slipping badly and release brake pressure. The driver can need more room to stop, with no warning that braking has weakened.

General Motors, which built the affected ZDXs, provided Honda with new information in October. Honda decided on October 29 to issue the recall and said it had received no warranty claims or reports of injuries or deaths tied to the issue as of that date.

GM also recently recalled 67,380 Cadillac and Chevrolet EVs over a brake software issue that can reduce braking at low speeds.

Acura will offer a free software update

Owners who have accepted the applicable terms can install the updated brake software over the air. Acura dealers can also install it free of charge.

You can read the full NHTSA recall notice below.

data.title: Most Torontonians are unlikely to ride in a Waymo, poll finds
data.description:
Waymo is already mapping Toronto’s streets ahead of a planned 2028 robotaxi launch, but a new poll suggests many residents would leave the driverless cars at the curb. Liaison Strategies surveyed 1,000 Torontonians on November 14 and 15 and found that 62% were unlikely to use the service.

There was more support for letting Waymo try out its technology – 64% backed testing with a safety driver behind the wheel. On the question of allowing Waymo to charge for rides with nobody in the driver’s seat, 51% were opposed and 36% were in favour.

A cheaper ride only goes so far

When asked to choose between a Waymo and a ride with a human driver, 71% picked the human driver if both rides cost $20 and arrived at the same time. Just 15% chose Waymo. Dropping the robotaxi fare by $5 raised its share to 27%, while 59% still opted for the human driver.

Asked what should happen next, 35% wanted supervised testing to continue without opening driverless rides to the public. Another 30% backed a pilot confined to parts of the city. Only 11% favoured an ongoing commercial service, while 18% wanted testing to stop altogether.

Snow and ice top the list of concerns

Winter driving was the most common concern, cited by 24% of respondents, followed by the safety of people walking and cycling at 22%. In a separate question, 45% said they thought driverless vehicles would make streets more dangerous for those road users, compared with 19% who expected safety to improve.

As Drive Tesla previously reported, Waymo’s Toronto rollout starts with people manually driving the cars to map local roads. The company plans to move from mapping to autonomous testing with a trained specialist at the wheel before launching its first Canadian service.

data.title: Waymo expands freeway pause across U.S. after California safety order
data.description:
Waymo’s freeway troubles now extend beyond California, with the company suspending freeway rides throughout its U.S. markets following the state DMV’s intervention.

The nationwide pause goes beyond what California regulators required. Waymo said it has also withdrawn freeway access elsewhere while reviewing its vehicles’ performance. Passengers can still book trips on city streets.

For riders, that means checking journey times before booking. Waymo’s support page now advises passengers to review their expected arrival time while freeway routes are unavailable. The company has not announced when those routes will return.

California order prompts wider pullback

California’s DMV imposed its restriction after identifying safety concerns involving construction areas and police traffic controls.

The agency cited three Waymo vehicles entering roadwork near Burlingame on Highway 101, along with a separate encounter where a robotaxi tried to get past highway patrol officers slowing traffic on I-280.

California’s order will remain until Waymo demonstrates that it has effectively corrected the problems. The broader suspension is a company decision, extending the pullback to markets outside the state.

Another interruption to freeway service

This follows an earlier voluntary pause in May, when Waymo withdrew freeway rides while improving its vehicles’ responses to construction zones. Service subsequently resumed after software changes.

Drive Tesla also covered a June recall involving freeway construction zones, following cases where robotaxis failed to recognize closures.

Waymo is now reviewing freeway performance across its markets while continuing local street service. Returning to California freeways will also require satisfying the DMV that its corrective measures work.

data.title: Canada’s EV sales jump 67% in September as four provinces set records
data.description:
Canada’s electric vehicle market picked up speed in September, with sales rising 66.6% from a year earlier. Nearly one in six new vehicles sold was a battery-electric model or a plug-in hybrid, and four provinces set records for EV market share.

The latest data from Statistics Canada shows Canadians purchased 28,490 new zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs) in September 2026, up 66.6% from a year earlier. Battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) and plug-in hybrids together accounted for 15.8% of the new-vehicle market, up from 10.1% last September. Overall vehicle sales grew 7% to 180,457. 

September also brought a sizeable jump from August, when Canadians bought 22,716 ZEVs and the segment accounted for 13% of new-vehicle sales. That works out to nearly 5,800 additional vehicles in a month and a 2.8-percentage-point gain in market share.

B.C. leads as Ontario hits 12%

British Columbia led the way in September, with EVs making up 28% of new vehicle sales. Ontario set its own record at 12%, and Alberta and Saskatchewan both hit new highs. In Quebec, EVs accounted for more than a quarter of new vehicle sales, the province’s best showing since 2024.

The September figures follow a strong third quarter for several automakers. As Drive Tesla previously reported, GM’s Canadian ZEV sales rose 118% year over year in Q3, while Toyota and Lexus sold a combined 10,114 ZEVs, a quarterly record for Toyota Canada. Both the Toyota bZ and bZ Woodland had their strongest quarters to date.

More EVs fall below $40,000 with the federal rebate

One of the obvious reasons for the increase is the return of federal incentives and a wider selection of lower-priced models. There are upwards of 11 EV models priced below $40,000 after the federal rebate, which offers up to $5,000 on eligible vehicles. 

The figures also come as B.C.’s incoming government weighs its next steps on the province’s Zero-Emission Vehicles Act. Clean Energy Canada says the law helps keep a broad selection of EVs available to buyers across the province.

data.title: Tesla Registers a Record 200 Cybercabs in Texas in One Day
data.description:
Tesla added 200 Cybercabs to its Texas Robotaxi registrations on Tuesday, its biggest one-day jump yet. That brings the company total to 773 Cybercabs and 734 Model Ys on the state register, putting Tesla back ahead of Waymo with 1,507 vehicles to Waymo’s 1,321.

The numbers come from the Texas DMV’s automated vehicle register, with the model breakdown based on VIN data. When we checked the numbers on November 9, Tesla was three vehicles behind Waymo. It now leads by 186.

Dallas is next in line for Cybercab rides

Austin is still the only city where riders can book a Cybercab, but those 773 registrations cover all of Texas. Based on what we know about the Austin fleet, the company isn’t operating nearly anywhere close to that number of Cybercabs in the city.

That means a good portion of the new registrations could be for Dallas, where Tesla already offers rides in Model Ys and where the company announced Cybercab is heading to next. That rollout is still pending, but recent footage shows dozens of gold Cybercabs parked in rows in a Dallas lot.

Houston is another place where Tesla has been building up its fleet. As we reported in October, drone footage showed an estimated 190 to 200 Cybercabs at Tesla’s Houston site, with some heading out on nearby roads for testing.

The registry doesn’t say where the latest 200 Cybercabs will go or how many are already in those lots. Still, with cars already on the ground in Dallas and Houston, there’s good reason to think some of the new registrations are for cities beyond Austin. Dallas is the one Tesla has given a launch window for.

data.title: Tesla opens first Megacharger in Texas as network expansion accelerates
data.description:
Tesla is wasting little time expanding its charging infrastructure for the Tesla Semi, opening its first public Megacharger in Texas less than a week after adding four new locations across the United States.

The newest Megacharger is located in Mesquite, just east of Dallas, and features eight charging stalls capable of delivering up to 1.2 megawatts (MW) of power each.

The opening follows a significant expansion of Tesla’s public Megacharger network last week, when new stations came online in Hodgkins, Illinois, Urbandale, Iowa, Ogallala, Nebraska, and Riverdale, Utah.

Those four additions nearly doubled the size of Tesla’s public Megacharger network. With the opening in Mesquite, the network has now grown from five to 10 locations in less than a month.

Tesla has also been working to speed up the construction of new charging stations, having introduced pre-assembled Megachargers in September. The prefabricated units combine a V4 power cabinet with two charging posts, reducing the amount of construction work required on-site.

Tesla builds out Semi infrastructure in Texas

Charging infrastructure isn’t the only thing Tesla is expanding in Texas. The company also recently opened its first dedicated Semi service centre in Laredo, near the border with Mexico and along one of the busiest commercial trucking corridors in the country.

Announcing the opening of the Mesquite Megacharger, Tesla Semi said the company is “rapidly scaling charging & service for Semi” in Texas.

Here in Canada, Tesla has also launched its Semi Charging for Business program, allowing Canadian companies to purchase and install their own Megachargers. B.C.-based R.R. Plett Trucking is already planning installations in Langley and Kamloops ahead of receiving its first 12 Tesla Semis in June 2027.
